messages.subject: Wald test
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to run a Wald test. Essentially I have a Heywood case for one of my latent variables where the variance for the latent is negative, but none of the individual indicators are negative. 



My model is below:

#install.packages("lavaan") #for SEM
library(lavaan)


mymodel <- '

#measurement model

ent =~ sdes_q1 + sdes_q4 +  sdes_q6 + sdes_q8

def =~ sdes_q2 + sdes_q3 + sdes_q5 + sdes_q7

idea =~ dssis_q1r + dssis_q2r + dssis_q3r + dssis_q4r

dep =~ cessds_q1 + cessds_q2 + cessds_q3 + cessds_q4 + cessds_q5r + cessds_q6 + cessds_q7 + cessds_q8r + cessds_q9 + cessds_q10


#structural model

def ~ dep

ent ~ def + dep

idea ~  ent + dep'


# model identification and estimation
modelfit <- sem(mymodel, data = mydatat1, estimator = "MLM") 

summary(modelfit_ideation, fit.measures = T, standardized = T, rsquare = T) 


The result gives me a negative error variance for ent only  (-0.011).

I can confirm too that there are no outliers on this variable (the distribution is actually somewhat bimodal with floor/ceiling effects). 

I've done some reading around Heywood cases, and I've seen that a Wald test can explore this further. I've run: 

lavTestWald(mymodel, "ent")

But this gives me an error: Error in lavParseModelString(constraints) : lavaan ERROR: model does not contain lavaan syntax (no operators found)


I'm otherwise pretty stuck - I've tried more simply YouTube videos etc, but there aren't any on how to handle Heywood cases specifically in R. 

Any help is really appreciated. 

Rosie

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Wald test
parts: I have a Heywood case

You can print the 95% CI instead:

summary(fit, ci = TRUE)

Then just check that the CI includes positive values (in which case you can't reject the H0 that the true residual variance > 0)

lavTestWald(mymodel, "ent")

You are not specifying a constraint to be tested.  If you label the parameter in the model syntax, then you can specify a constraint that this parameter == 0 (or a small, positive number, but again the CI is easier because it is the entire range of H0 values that cannot be rejected by the data).  See the help-page for examples.
